*J U D G M E N T

* This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioner U/S 166 of M.V. Act, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/ on account of the injuries sustained by him, in a road traffic accident.

*FACTS OF THE CASE IN NUTSHELL*
2.

Facts leading to the case of the petitioner forthcoming in the petition that, on an unfortunate date on 28.2.2021 at about 12:30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding in his Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA40EE8096, near Narepalli Cross, NH44 Road, Bagepalli Taluk,
Chickballapura, Karnataka.

At that time, the driver of the Car bearing Registration No.TN07FR 2498, came from behind, in a rash and negligent manner with high speed, thereby lost control and dashed against petitioner's motor cycle.
Consequently, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

3. It is stated that, immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Government hospital, Bagepalli and after taking first aid treatment, he was shifted to M.S.Ramaiah hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took inpatient treatment.
He spent Rs.10,00,000/ towards treatment, medicines, nourishment and conveyance charges.
4. It is stated that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy, and he was aged about 60 years and was doing Barbar work and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/ per month.
Due to the accident, the petitioner had suffered mental and physical as well as financial hardship.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, accident was purely on account of the negligence of the driver of the Car bearing Registration No.TS07FR2498.

In this regard, case was registered against the driver by the jurisdictional Bagepalli police as per Crime being the owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Accordingly,
petitioner has filed the instant petition, claiming compensation.

6. After service of the notice of this petition, though respondent No.1 appeared through her counsel,
but not filed written statement, in answer to the case of the petitioner.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 had appeared before the Court through counsel and filed written statement, in answer to the case of the petitioner.

Sri. A.Gopalappa vs )Smt. Lakshmi Tapala on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102858179/
2 7.
The respondent No.2, in the written statement has not seriously disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner.

But, strongly denied the allegation of actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle and admitted about the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the offending car bearing registration No.TS07FR2498 in favour of the respondent No.1, as on the date of the accident, subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further,
contended that, neither the owner nor the police complied the mandatory provisions as required under section 134(c) and section 158(6) of the Motor Vehicles Act in furnishing the better particulars.
The main contention of the respondent No.2 that the jurisdictional police have filed false charge sheet against the insured vehicle by colluding with claimant and insured.

And contended that, there is two days delay in lodging the complaint, which clearly shows that, the petitioner in colluding with the jurisdictional police, have set up and fixed the alleged vehicle in question, which was not involved in the accident at all.
It is stated that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid DL, as on the date of the accident and thereby the owner of the vehicle violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
As such, the respondent is not liable to pay any compensation.

It is specifically contended that, the alleged accident occurred solely due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner, who came from the wrong side/opposite direction and hit to some other vehicles.
And the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against their company.
8. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, for final determination of the case, framed the following:
* ISSUES

* 
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in motor vehicles accident, that was taken place on 28.2.2021 at about 12.30 p.m., at Narepalli Cross, NH44 Road, Bagepalli Taluk, Chickballapura, Karnataka, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing registration No.TS 07FR2498 in an actionable negligence ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?

9. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner, by name Sri.A.Gopalappa, during the course of his evidence, placed his affidavit evidence, in lieu of examinationinchief, who examined as PW1 in the case on hand.
At the time of his evidence, 10 documentary evidence got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.
In addition to his evidence Dr.Yashavantha Kumar.C, was examined as PW2.
At the time of his evidence, 3 documentary evidence got marked as Ex.P11 to Ex.P13, for consideration.
10. On the other hand, the respondent No.2, except filing written statement has not adduced rebuttal evidence for consideration to prove all the defenses forthcoming in its written statement.
And the respondent No.1, neither filed written statement, nor adduced evidence.

Hence, matter was Sri. A.Gopalappa vs )Smt. Lakshmi Tapala on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102858179/
3 set down for arguments.
11. Heard the argument of both the counsel.
And perused the materials available on record.

At the time of argument, learned counsel for the respondent No.2 filed written arguments and also relied on the following authorities for consideration, 1) ILR 2009 KAR 385 between Smt. Nasreen Banu &
Others Vs Divisional Manager & Another 2) MFA No.30284/2008(MV), High Court of Karnataka,
Gulbarga Bench dated 5.12.2012 between Ramalingappa Vs Shivarao & others and 3) 2005 ACJ 1323 SC at New Delhi dated 18.4.2005 between National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs Prembai Patel and others.

sentences.text: 12. with due respect, I have gone through the propositions laid down in the said authorities, with respect to the proof of claim petition based on actionable negligence and observed that, it need not be proved, beyond reasonable doubt like, that of a penal action cases, and it is purely based on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
And also with respect to the liability of the insurance company and the owner of the offending vehicle.

13. On appreciation of the evidence available on record, my findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, For the following:

R E A S O N S ISSUE NO.1:
14.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle Car bearing registration No.TS07FR2498, alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

On the other hand, it is the strong contention of the respondent No.2 company that, alleged accident was caused due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner, and there is a violation of the terms and conditions of the policy and also contended that, the rider of the motor cycle was not holding valid and driving licence at the time of accident and was not wearing helmet.
As such, the petitioner is solely responsible for the accident and its consequences.
15. The petitioner-Gopalappa.A, herein, to discharge the burden lies on him, placed his affidavit evidence and examined as PW1.
At the time of his evidence, placed 10 documentary evidence for consideration.
Apart from this, relied on the evidence of PW1 and documentary evidence Ex.P.11 to Ex.P.13, in order to prove the injuries sustained by him in the accident.
Among the documents placed by the petitioner, Ex.P.1 to Ex.
P.6 are the material documents for consideration to prove the above issue.
On the other hand, to prove all the defenses forthcoming in the written statement of the respondent No.2, not adduced any rebuttal evidence and to answer the case of the petitioner.

Hence,
duty is more on the part of the court, to assess the evidence carefully, in order to come to the proper conclusion.

Sri. A.Gopalappa vs )Smt. Lakshmi Tapala on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102858179/
4 16.
To demonstrate all the assertions forthcoming in the evidence of the PW1

, the petitioner herein,
as discussed above, placed police papers as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.6.
On taking birds eye view towards the recitals of the documents, reflect that, alleged accident had taken placed 28.2.2021.
And information in this regard was received from the son of the petitioner by name Manjunath.Y.G.

In connection with delay of 4 days in giving first information is concerned, in the Ex.P.1 column No.3 (c), and in the recitals of the complaint Ex.P.2, there is a clear narration that, since the complainant was providing treatment to his father, belated complaint was given.
This reason remained unquestioned by the other side.

When the petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident, one cannot expect immediate complaint from his family members, without giving concentration about providing treatment to the petitioner.
Hence, delay in giving first information in the case on hand, is not fatal.

17. It is also pertinent note herein that, in the light of the first information given by the complainant,
criminal law set in motion against the driver of the car bearing registration No.TS07FR 2498 alleging that, he has committed the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC.
This document remained unquestioned by the other side.
In the recitals of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, there is a clear narration about the negligent act on the part of the driver of the car, to cause the accident and its consequences.

In order to eradicate the recitals of these two material documents, the driver of the offending vehicle has not made an effort to question these documents, well in time before the competent court of law.

18. Added to this, on going through the spot mahazar marked at Ex.P.3, executed by the investigation officer, after setting criminal law in motion against the driver of the offending vehicle reflect that, there is an involvement of this vehicle in the accident and the said document was executed in the presence of complainant and panch witnesses.

Ex. P.4, opinion of the Motor vehicle inspector depict that, accident in question was not due any mechanical defects of the vehicles involved in the accident, and the damages noted in the said document, was not seriously disputed.

Further, the recitals of wound certificate Ex.P.5, goes to show that, consequent upon the accident,
the petitioner had sustained grievous injury.
To disbelieve the recitals of all these documents no rebuttal evidence from the side of the respondents herein.

19. Ultimately, on going through the final report submitted by the investigation officer and the recitals of the column No.17 of said document, goes to show that, the said charge sheet submitted against the driver of the offending vehicle by name Sheikh Akbar alleging that, he had committed the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 338 of IPC.

This material document though not substantive piece of evidence in proof of claim petition, in the absence of contra materials, that document can be considered as conclusive proof, with respect to the proof of the fact in issue, about the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner .

20. As already discussed above, no rebuttal evidence from the side of the respondents, in answer to the case of the petitioner and at the time of cross examination of PW1, though several questions put to the witness, to prove the innocence of the driver of the offending vehicle and to prove the defense that, there was a negligence on the part of the petitioner, nothing worthwhile is elicited to Sri. A.Gopalappa vs )Smt. Lakshmi Tapala on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102858179/
5 suspect about the case of the petitioner and also to show that, the petitioner has engineered the prosecution papers for the sake of compensation.
Hence, the evidence adduced by the petitioner is to be accepted as per law.
21. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, I am of the view that, the petitioner had placed convincing and reliable evidence, to prove the fact in issue, in the case on hand.
The respondent No.2 has utterly failed to shaken the evidence of the petitioner, and to prove the defenses, through rebuttal evidence.
Accordingly, I am of the view that, the alleged accident had occurred, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing registration No.TS07FR2498.

Hence,
without making much discussion on the point of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the Issue No.1, in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2 :
22.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of relief claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/ on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident, under different heads.

23. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.

Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.

entities.text: Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavoring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.

"
24. In connection with the injuries sustained by the petitioner, has produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P5.

The said document discloses that, he sustained the following injuries:
1. Laceration, oblique, right mid 1/ 3 rd leg, 12x3 cms, fresh bleeding +  fracture leg bones xray shows segmental right tibia and fibula fractures.
Later open reduction & internal fixation was done 25.
According to the doctor, said injury is grievous in nature.

To substantiate the said fact, the petitioner has placed, discharge summary as per Ex.P.7, 22 medical bills and 13 prescriptions as per Sri. A.Gopalappa vs )Smt. Lakshmi Tapala on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102858179/
6 Ex.P.9 and Ex.P.10 respectively.

In addition to the evidence of PW2, produced inpatient record,
two outpatient record and Xray as per Ex.P11 to Ex.P.13.
On going through the discharge summary of M.S.Ramaiah hospital, Bengaluru marked as per Ex.P.7, the petitioner was admitted to the hospital as an inpatient on 28.2.2021 and discharged on 9.3.2021.

For having taken note of the nature of the injury sustained by the petitioner and by keeping in mind about the sufferings of the petitioner and also the evidence given by the PW2, about the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner and mode of treatment given to him, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/ towards pain and suffering.
26. Another point to be discussed herein, about the loss of income during laid up period and rest period, is concerned,
In the petition, the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident, he was working as a Barbar and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/ per month.
But, he has not placed any iota of documents to show the definite income of Rs.20,000/ per month.
On the other hand, it is to be noted that, the injury sustained by him is, grievous in nature, as per the wound certificate.
On going through the discharge summary of M.S.Ramaiah hospital,Bengaluru marked as per Ex.P.7, the petitioner was admitted to the hospital as an inpatient on 28.2.2021 and discharged on 9.3.2021.
Hence, definitely, there was some difficulty to him, during the period of treatment, to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for one month.
At the time of fracture, it is very difficult for him, to do his work, as he was earlier during the period of treatment.
Hence, I am of the view that, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/ towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

27. The petitioner herein, in connection with his treatment expenses, at the time of his evidence,
placed 22 medical bills of Rs.1,06,350/ along with 13 prescriptions as per Ex.P9 and Ex.P10.
In connection with the said medical bills, except the suggestion that, the said documents are created documents, no contra materials placed, to disbelieve the said documents.
On going through the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, and mode of treatment taken by him, will not create suspicion to disbelieve the said documents.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,06,350/ under the head of medical expenses.
28. The petitioner herein, as per the medical records, had sustained grevious injury.

And took treatment at M.S.Ramaiah hospital, Bengaluru as per Ex.P.7 - discharge summary, the petitioner was admitted to the hospital as an inpatient on 28.2.2021 and discharged on 9.3.2021 i.e. for 10 days.

As such, during the period of treatment, he could have spent some amount towards travelling,
food and nourishment.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/ towards attendant charges, food, and nourishment and conveyance charges.
29. Another material point of loss of future income is concerned, the petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.
In the evidence of the PW1, reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P5, goes to show that, he had sustained one grievous injury.
To substantiate this, the petitioner had placed, wound certificate, and discharge summary, medical bills and prescription.

But, on taking birds eye view towards said documents,
disclose about gravity of the injuries sustained by the petitioner.

Apart from this, placed the Sri. A.Gopalappa vs )Smt. Lakshmi Tapala on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102858179/
7 evidence of the doctor by name Dr.Yashwantha Kumar.C, who examined as PW2.
30.

In the evidence of PW2, deposed that, on the history of RTA, the petitioner had sustained,
Type 3A open segmental fracture of both bones right leg.
In this regard, he underwent procedure of closed reduction and intra medullary nailing of tibia under spinal anesthesia on 1.3.2021.
Further he deposed that, post operative period patient was uneventful and he was discharged on 9.3.2021.
Further, during the follow up period, it was noticed that, fractures are united, he has stiffness in the joints and difficulty in squatting and sitting cross legged.

On clinical and radiological assessment on examination of the petitioner on 29.11.2022, as per the guidelines of National gazette, PW2 has assessed on various points with respect to mobility and stability components and by taking into consideration of other aspects, came to the conclusion that, combined mobility and stability is at 30+23 (90 23) 90 = 47%.
Combined value for right lower limb is 47% and whole body is at 15%
and also opined that, the petitioner requires another surgery in the form of implant removal which will cost approximately of Rs.60,000/.
In support of the evidence of PW2 produced Ex.P.11 to Ex.P.13 for consideration.
31. At the time of crossexamination of PW2, admitted that, he was not given wound certificate.
But, in their hospital MLC was executed, and he is the treated doctor of the petitioner.

As per his answers, on the same day of the accident, the petitioner had been to their hospital, at that time,
there was a fracture in the tibia and fibula of the petitoner.

But, no fracture with respect to hip,
femur and ankle.
And answered that, at present, both the fractures are united and the movement of the hip of the petitioner at present is in order.
And denied the suggestion that, knee and ankle movements are also are in order.

Further, he answered that, implants of the petitioner not yet removed by denying the suggestion that, if at all the implants are removed, no difficulty will be caused to the petitioner and his percentage of disability will be reduced.
And admitted that, he has not given disability certificate to the petitioner and not advised for further treatment.

And denied the suggestion of other side that, the petitioner is suffering only 10% of the disability and denied the suggestion that, he assessed the disability and expressed his opinion about future medical expenses in higher side only to help the petitioner.
32. Over all appreciation of the evidence of PW2, along with entire medical documents pertaining to the petitioner coupled with the appreciation of the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and mode of treatment taken by him, I am of the view of that, percentage of the disability expressed by the PW2, in connection with the whole body of the petitioner, seems little bit exorbitant.
Hence, it is apt to take the percentage of disability as 12% instead of 15%.
The same will meet the ends of justice.
33. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 60 years.
To prove the age, he had placed Aadhaar card marked as per Ex.P.8.
In the said document, date of birth of the petitioner has been mentioned as 20.06.1960.
The accident was occurred on 28.2.2021.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the age of the petitioner is to be considered as 61 years.
To the sai0d age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '7' is to be taken into consideration.

Sri. A.Gopalappa vs )Smt. Lakshmi Tapala on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102858179/
8 34.

Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in the main petition, and also in the examinationinchief evidence, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, prior to the accident, he was doing Barbar work and was earning Rs.20,000/ per month.
In this regard, no iota of evidence has been placed to show that, he was earning Rs.20,000/ per month prior to the date of accident.
In such a situation, as per law, notional income has to be taken in to consideration.
But, the said notional income has to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, in the case on hand, alleged accident had taken place in the year 2021.

As per the notional income chart, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.15,000/
for the year 2021.

35. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.15,000X12X7 X 12/100 = Rs.1,51,200/
36.

Next factual aspect loss of amenities is concerned, due to the accidental injuries, definitely, the petitioner will suffer in a slight manner in future, while doing his day today activities as well as to do his avocation for his livelihood.
On going through the work of the petitioner, there may be some functional disability to him, consequent upon the injuries.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.20,000/ towards loss of amenities.

37. In connection with the future medication expenses is concerned, the PW2 at the time of his evidence, stated that the petitioner needs surgery for removal of implant which would cost around Rs.60,000/.
But, no estimation placed in this regard, to have an idea about the definite expenses towards future medical expenses.

Hence, by taking into consideration of the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/ under the head of future medication.

38. In view of my due discussions held above, on various aspects, the petitioner is entitled for compensation in toto, under the following heads:
Compensation heads
Compensation amount 1. Pain and Suffering Rs. 50,00000 2. Loss of income during Rs. 15,00000 laidup period and rest period 3.

Medical expenses Rs. 1,06,35000 4.Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 10,00000 and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income Rs. 1,51,20000 Sri. A.Gopalappa vs )Smt. Lakshmi Tapala on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102858179/
9 6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 20,00000
7.Future Medical expenses Rs. 20,00000 Total Rs.3,72,55000 39.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,72,550/, (Rupees Three Lakhs,
Seventy Two Thousand, Five Hundred and Fifty only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in MFA No.103557/2016,
Between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated.
20.03.2018.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: And MFA No.30131/2019 dated.12.5.2020, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount

. 
LIABILITY:
40.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing registration No.TS07FR2498,
alleged accident had taken place.
As such, the respondent No.1, being the owner and the respondent No.2, being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

41. On the other hand, the respondent No.2, being the Insurance Company, not disputed the existence of the insurance policy, as on the date of the accident, and not produced any documents or evidence to show that, there is a violation of the terms and conditions of the Insurance policy.

As per the records, policy pertaining to the offending vehicle was valid from 23.2.2021 to 22.2.2022,
alleged accident had taken place on 28.2.2021.
42.
Accordingly, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.2, being the indemnifier has to pay compensation to the petitioner along with the interest at 6% per annum from the date of the petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
43.

In view of above discussion on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
*O R D E R* The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.
Consequently, the petitioner is entitled for compensation Rs.3,72,550/, (Rupees Three Lakhs,
Seventy Two Thousand, Five Hundred and Fifty only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.
Expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.

Sri. A.Gopalappa vs )Smt. Lakshmi Tapala on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102858179/
10
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any nationalized/ Schedule bank in F.D for a period of 3 years.
And remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.500/.
Draw award accordingly.

In this regard, case was registered against the driver by the jurisdictional Bagepalli police as per Crime being the owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

petitioner has filed the instant petition, claiming compensation.
The respondent No.2, in the written statement has not seriously disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner.
But, strongly denied the allegation of actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle and admitted about the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the offending car bearing registration No.TS07FR2498 in favour of the respondent No.1, as on the date of the accident, subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.
contended that, neither the owner nor the police complied the mandatory provisions as required under section 134(c) and section 158(6) of the Motor Vehicles Act in furnishing the better particulars.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Hence,
duty is more on the part of the court, to assess the evidence carefully, in order to come to the proper conclusion.
To demonstrate all the assertions forthcoming in the evidence of the PW1
In connection with delay of 4 days in giving first information is concerned, in the Ex.P.1 column No.3 (c), and in the recitals of the complaint Ex.P.2, there is a clear narration that, since the complainant was providing treatment to his father, belated complaint was given.
When the petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident, one cannot expect immediate complaint from his family members, without giving concentration about providing treatment to the petitioner.
Hence, delay in giving first information in the case on hand, is not fatal.
In the recitals of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, there is a clear narration about the negligent act on the part of the driver of the car, to cause the accident and its consequences.
In order to eradicate the recitals of these two material documents, the driver of the offending vehicle has not made an effort to question these documents, well in time before the competent court of law.
19. Ultimately, on going through the final report submitted by the investigation officer and the recitals of the column No.17 of said document, goes to show that, the said charge sheet submitted against the driver of the offending vehicle by name Sheikh Akbar alleging that, he had committed the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 338 of IPC.
This material document though not substantive piece of evidence in proof of claim petition, in the absence of contra materials, that document can be considered as conclusive proof, with respect to the proof of the fact in issue, about the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner .
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
Hence, I am of the view that, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/ towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the age of the petitioner is to be considered as 61 years.
In this regard, no iota of evidence has been placed to show that, he was earning Rs.20,000/ per month prior to the date of accident.
In such a situation, as per law, notional income has to be taken in to consideration.
But, the said notional income has to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.20,000/ towards loss of amenities.
Hence, by taking into consideration of the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/ under the head of future medication.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.500/.
